solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.note: 'One's quick' reads as 'one that is quick', a noun phrase for the fast car

blocks.note: to sport something is to display it, as in sporting a new hat
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone eager to show off a mark, perhaps a grade or a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks like a possessive but is 'one is': the definition is a thing that is quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a car built for speed is the one that's quick.

clue.text: Apartment delightful, by the sound of it? (5)

indicators.note: 'by the sound of it' tells us to take the word as it is heard, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: sweet = delightful; the answer is spelt differently but said the same

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a flat and calling it delightful, going by what they have heard.
explanation.walkthrough: SUITE and SWEET are pronounced the same, so the sweet-sounding word is spelt as the set of rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a set of connected rooms, as in a hotel, is an apartment.

clue.text: Quick to respond, getting one’s kicks? (2,3,4)

definitions.note: a playful description of a footballer kicking the ball; a phrase, not a direct synonym

blocks.note: alert and sharp
read literally: a footballer with the ball at their feet, kicking it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's kicks' usually means having fun; here it is literal — a player in possession of the ball is ON THE BALL, kicking it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone alert and quick to react is on the ball, and the second sense is the literal footballing one.

clue.text: Small groups here written about, first of several in books (10)

indicators.note: 'written about' suggests the letters of 'here' are moved about when set down
'first of several' keeps only the opening letter of 'several'
the letters go 'in' the books, so the books word wraps around them

blocks.note: the word itself, taken as letters to rearrange
the first letter of 'several'
tomes are books, usually big ones

explanation.surface: A note that small groups have been written about in several books.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert goes in after the first letter of the books, not in the middle. 'Written about' sounds like literary coverage, but it only stirs the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: groups of three are about as small as groups get.

clue.text: Lift and tilt up part of plane (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means read the word from the bottom

blocks.note: to cock is to raise or turn upward, as in cocking an ear or a hat
to tip is to tilt

explanation.surface: Instructions for lifting and tilting a section of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tilt up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' only tells us to reverse TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the pilot's compartment at the front is one part of an aircraft.

indicators.note: letters that are incorrect are in the wrong order and need rearranging

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A question of whether a chute is correct or incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' reads as a choice between correct and incorrect, but it is fodder alongside CHUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: touching up a picture or text corrects its small flaws.

indicators.note: a reversible answer reads the same when turned round

blocks.note: the letters read the same backwards as forwards

explanation.surface: A building or framework that can be flipped round.
explanation.walkthrough: The only wordplay is that PUTUP reads the same in either direction, so the definition does all the work and the crossers confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to erect a shed or tent is to construct it.

indicators.note: the word contracts, getting shorter by its last letter

blocks.note: a plant is a factory; it loses its final T

explanation.surface: A factory drawing up contracts in draft form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun, legal papers, but it is a verb: PLANT shrinks by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a draft is a preliminary scheme, and drafting is scheming it out.

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A drunk high on marijuana shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On marijuana' reads as 'high', but 'on' is RE, joined to POT, and the whole REPOT then goes upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, if an old-fashioned one: a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Saint passing round cupola, one can tell how far he walked? (9)

definitions.text: one can tell how far he walked
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the device rather than a synonym

indicators.note: the saint goes round the cupola, enclosing it

blocks.note: St Peter
a cupola is a small dome

explanation.surface: A saint walking around a domed building, with someone counting his steps.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'he' who walked seems to be the saint of the surface, but in the definition it is anyone wearing the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a step-counting device can tell its wearer the distance walked.

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to Milan's other football club rather than a synonym

blocks.note: to place a body in a grave
Milan's other big football club, Internazionale

explanation.surface: An exasperated shout about which football club Bury is, or is not.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also an English town with a football club, which sets the football scene. Milan has two big clubs: AC Milan and Inter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for burying a body, plus a proper name found by elimination between Milan's two clubs.

clue.text: Beaten about at start of night, rested for a while (9)

indicators.note: the 'beaten' word is placed about the other letters, surrounding them
'start of night' keeps only its first letter

blocks.note: to cap is to beat or outdo, as in capping a story
the word itself
the first letter of 'night'

explanation.surface: Someone knocked about early in the night, then resting for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' suggests a violent scene, but it means surpassed, as in capping someone's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a catnap is a short doze, so taking one is resting for a while.

definitions.note: a playful description: the side's players with the subs added

blocks.note: the British school entrance exam
a football side is eleven players; add the subs and you have more

explanation.surface: Trying out a football side, bench players included.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus is a British exam once taken at age 11 to decide entry to grammar school. A football team is an eleven, and with its substitutes it is eleven plus.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name for one particular exam, and a cryptic description of a squad.

indicators.note: 'money, primarily' keeps just the first letter of 'money'

blocks.note: pro = for, in favour of
the first letter of 'money'

explanation.surface: Someone dancing mainly for the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' seems to mean 'mainly' but only takes the first letter of 'money'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the formal end-of-year school ball is one kind of dance.

indicators.note: abandoned also means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A roguish country squire who has thrown off his cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like it drops the cape, but no letters are lost: it means wild, and all ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: picaresque fiction follows a lovable rogue's adventures, so the word means roguish.

blocks.note: at top speed
British slang for exhausted

explanation.surface: Something broken to pieces in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' pretends to mean smashed but is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Two idioms: going as fast as possible, and lying worn out.

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: if = provided (that)
William Sherman, the American Civil War general

explanation.surface: Asking for a pay rise from a general for someone who works with nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' looks like a pay rise but is an instruction to turn IF upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the hyphenated coinage names someone whose work is done with nets.

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: MANE with its last letter cut

blocks.note: a bob is a short, straight hairstyle
a lion's mane with its last letter cut off leaves 'man'

explanation.surface: Asking whether Bob is the lion's keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A lion's mane is its hair; cut the E from MANE and 'man' is left, so 'lion's man' is a HAIR CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example (a bob is one style), plus a cryptic reading of the lion's shortened mane.

clue.text: Chapati about to be stuffed with short old sausage (9)

indicators.note: the chapati is turned about, its letters moved
a short word loses its last letter
the rearranged chapati is filled with the other letters

blocks.note: the word itself, as letters to rearrange
OLD cut short, losing its D

explanation.surface: A flatbread wrapped round an old sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: The flatbread and the sausage share a scene, so 'Chapati' looks like mere setting; in fact it supplies seven of the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small, thin British sausage is one kind of sausage.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Praise for the remarkable stories within a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' pretends to be a book but means new.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something prominent or striking is worth remarking on.

clue.text: About a hundred red hot switches lit up (7)

indicators.note: the red-hot letters go about C, around it
the letters switch places

blocks.note: the words themselves
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Around a hundred glowing switches light up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switches' looks like light switches, fitting 'lit up', but it is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: setting something alight lights it up.

clue.text: Listener involved in row getting more upset (7)

indicators.note: the listener is involved in, placed inside, the row

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the ear is what listens

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in an argument becoming more distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' sounds like an argument, fitting the upset listener, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative synonym: closer to tears means more upset.

clue.text: Where inpatients are taken, just before (7)

definitions.note: a phrase, split as two words, not a synonym

blocks.note: hospital patients are taken to the rooms of beds where they stay
near in time, as in '___ midnight'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TO WARDS: hospital inpatients are taken to wards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic split into two words, and a plain sense of nearing a point in time.

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round

blocks.note: equipped (to do something) = able

explanation.surface: An island ready to stage a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The island Napoleon was exiled to is a nice fit for a surface about revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Mediterranean island off Italy.

blocks.note: short for Buckinghamshire, an English county
as in going against a trend

explanation.walkthrough: The county name is the usual short form of Buckinghamshire, northwest of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviated proper name, and a plain verb synonym for going against something.

blocks.note: British slang for fed up
cooking: food finished under a grill until its surface colours

explanation.surface: Someone irritated after being interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilled' pretends to mean questioned hard, but here it is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang idiom for irritation, and a literal cooking description.

clue.text: Mock exams seeming laughable at first, initially upset (5)

indicators.note: 'initially' takes the first letter of each word
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

blocks.note: first letters of Exams Seeming Laughable At First

explanation.surface: Practice exams that seemed a joke at first, leaving the student upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like an indicator next to 'initially', but its two words are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mock leather is imitation, not genuine.

clue.text: Play about Romeo where great beauty held captive (4)

indicators.note: the play word goes about Romeo, around it

blocks.note: to toy is to play
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A play about Romeo, set where a beauty was held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'Romeo' conjure Shakespeare, but the play is the verb TOY and Romeo is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Helen, the great beauty of Greek legend, was kept in the besieged city.

clue.text: General damage filing account a day later (9)

indicators.note: the account is filed into the damage word, put inside it
the day comes later, after the rest

blocks.note: to mar is to damage
AC is the abbreviation for account
THUR is short for Thursday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: Damage from filing an account a day late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' leads the clue as if an adjective, but it is the definition, a military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Douglas MacArthur was a US general in the Second World War.

definitions.note: a layer here is something that lays eggs

blocks.note: to flinch or shrink back in fear
a small game bird that lays eggs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' reads as a stratum, but it is something that lays: a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym for recoiling, and a definition by example of an egg-laying bird.

clue.text: Vicious characters in inquisition as tyrannous? (5)

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters sitting in the next words

blocks.note: inquisitioN AS TYrannous

explanation.surface: Cruel figures in an inquisition, as tyrannical as they come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' pretends to be people, the inquisitors, but it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean cruel or spiteful.

indicators.note: reckless letters are thrown about carelessly

blocks.note: the first 'speed' is itself; the second is RATE, a speed

explanation.surface: A warning chant about driving too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mirrors itself: 'Reckless' is the definition and 'reckless' the anagram indicator, with 'speed' once as itself and once as RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acting without care for risk.
